questions.statement: What are the "3 Rs" of the environment?

options.feedback: Incorrect. These are general activities.
Correct! These are the three pillars of environmental waste management.

options.feedback: Incorrect. These are usually composted, not recycled in the standard sense.

questions.statement: "When you use a plastic bottle again as a plant pot, you are ________ it."

options.feedback: Incorrect. Reducing means using less of it.
Correct! Using an item again for a new purpose is "reusing".
Incorrect. Recycling involves breaking down the material to make something new.
Incorrect. You are keeping it.

questions.explanation:
The student understands the specific distinction between reusing and other waste management actions.

options.feedback: Incorrect. While they can be, it's not the defining characteristic here.

questions.statement: How are the students practicing "Reduce" in the project?
questions.context:
A description of a "Zero Waste" project.

"The school started a Zero Waste project. Students bring their own water bottles and use digital notebooks. They also have a compost bin for fruit remains."

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is for organic waste management.

options.text: By using digital notebooks to use less paper.
options.feedback: Correct! Using less of a material (paper) is a form of reducing.
Incorrect. They are composting them.
Incorrect. They bring their own (reusable) ones.

questions.explanation:
The student applies reading comprehension to categorize a specific action within the "3 Rs" framework.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "A sustainable home ________ use solar panels to produce its own electricity."

options.feedback: 'Shouldn't use' would advise against solar panels, which is the opposite of what a sustainable home should do.
'Can use' states a possibility, which is exactly what a sustainable home has: solar panels producing its own electricity.
'Mustn't use' forbids solar panels, the opposite of the sustainability goal described.
'Isn't' is not a modal verb, so it cannot precede the base form 'use' in this structure.

questions.explanation:
The student applies knowledge of sustainable practices using the appropriate modal verb for possibility.

options.text: It is more expensive than making new paper.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Not mentioned.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: According to this definition, which action is sustainable?
questions.context:
Evaluating the definition of sustainability.

"Sustainability means meeting our own needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs."

options.text: Using all the available water today because we are thirsty.
options.feedback: Using all the water today leaves nothing for future generations, which is what the definition rules out.

options.text: Cutting down all the forests to build many houses quickly.
options.feedback: Cutting down the forests destroys a resource that future generations need to survive.

options.text: Using resources carefully so that there is enough for people in 50 years.
options.feedback: Using resources carefully so that there is enough for people in 50 years is exactly what the definition asks for: meeting present needs without compromising future ones.

options.text: Ignoring the environment because technology will solve everything.
options.feedback: Ignoring the environment relies on hope rather than on careful management, so it does not meet the definition.

questions.explanation: The student evaluates behaviors against a formal definition of sustainability to identify the most responsible action.
